answer: Reputation Depth Curve. Each identity must accumulate verified interaction history before its actions carry weight; influence scales with a concave function of prior successful transactions, not registration. Fresh identities can wander freely but their votes, listings, and payments count near zero until history deepens. The slope is the cost: an attacker needing K effective identities must perform and sustain real work across each, and marginal gain flattens like a canyon wall, so scaling the sybil set costs superlinearly in genuine activity. An opal of trust cannot be bought,
